UADataType.Description: Where inference executes. The result contract is identical in every case; this property exists so a client can reason about latency, availability and the trust boundary without changing how it reads results.

Field.Name: OnServer
Field.Description: In the OPC UA Server process or on its host.

Field.Name: EdgeOffServer
Field.Description: On a separate edge node reached over the network.

Field.Name: Cloud
Field.Description: In a remote or cloud service.

Field.Name: InSimulator
Field.Description: Inside a simulator that also produces the input.

UADataType.Description: Compute device executing the model.
Runtime lifecycle state of a deployment.

Field.Name: Inactive
Field.Description: Declared but not serving.

Field.Name: Ready
Field.Description: Able to serve; no work in progress.

Field.Name: Active
Field.Description: Serving at least one request.

Field.Name: Degraded
Field.Description: Serving below configured quality.

Field.Name: Faulted
Field.Description: Unable to serve.

UADataType.Description: Provenance of the samples in a dataset.

Field.Name: Real
Field.Description: Captured from physical equipment.

Field.Name: Synthetic
Field.Description: Generated or rendered by a simulator.

Field.Name: Mixed
Field.Description: Both, for example synthetic pre-training with real fine-tuning.

UADataType.Description: State of a dataset-capture, retraining and promotion cycle.

Field.Name: Ready
Field.Description: A candidate model is available for promotion.

UADataType.Description: Why an inference call stopped producing output. A client that treats every non-error response as complete will silently accept a truncated one, which is why this is Mandatory on a response rather than a diagnostic.

Field.Name: Stop
Field.Description: The model finished normally.

Field.Name: Length
Field.Description: Output was truncated by a length or budget limit. The result is incomplete and SHALL NOT be treated as final.

Field.Name: ToolCall
Field.Description: The model requested a tool or function call and is waiting for its result.

Field.Name: Filtered
Field.Description: Output was withheld by a safety policy; see the SafetyAssessment.

Field.Name: Cancelled
Field.Description: The caller or the Server cancelled the call.

Field.Name: Error
Field.Description: The call failed; the StatusCode carries the reason.

UADataType.Description: Wire contract a remote inference endpoint speaks. A Server needs this to call an endpoint it did not deploy; without it EndpointUri is a string nobody can act on. It describes the REMOTE endpoint and never affects how an OPC UA client calls this Server.

Field.Name: OpcUaInference
Field.Description: Another OPC UA Server implementing this specification's Invoke Method.

Field.Name: RestChatCompletions
Field.Description: The de-facto REST contract for chat and embeddings that most serving runtimes expose, including ones that run on a single workstation.

Field.Name: OpenInferenceProtocol
Field.Description: The Open Inference Protocol (KServe v2) predict contract.

Field.Name: TensorRemoteProcedure
Field.Description: A tensor-oriented RPC contract such as those used by dedicated inference servers.

Field.Name: EmbeddedRuntime
Field.Description: An in-process runtime reached through a local library rather than a network protocol.

Field.Name: Proprietary
Field.Description: A contract this specification does not name. EndpointDescriptionUri SHOULD then say where it is documented.

UADataType.Description: How the Server authenticates ITSELF to a remote inference endpoint. This is not how a client authenticates to this Server, which is the ordinary OPC UA Session security and is unaffected.

Field.Name: Anonymous
Field.Description: No credential. Permitted only where the endpoint is reachable solely from a trusted network segment.

Field.Name: ApiKey
Field.Description: A shared secret presented as a key.

Field.Name: BearerToken
Field.Description: A token obtained from an authorization service.

Field.Name: WorkloadIdentity
Field.Description: An identity the hosting platform assigns to the Server, so no secret is stored at all. Preferred where the platform offers it.

Field.Name: MutualTls
Field.Description: Both ends present certificates.

UADataType.Description: What the Server does when a deployment cannot serve. This is the question a plant asks that no cloud inference API answers, because a cloud API assumes the caller can simply wait.

Field.Name: Fail
Field.Description: Report the failure to the caller and produce nothing. The safe default: a caller that is told nothing happened can decide for itself.

Field.Name: HoldLast
Field.Description: Continue reporting the most recent successful result, marked stale. Legitimate only where a stale answer is safe, and the caller SHALL be able to see the staleness.

Field.Name: FallBackTo
Field.Description: Route to the deployment named by the FallsBackTo reference. The answer comes from a different model and the response SHALL say so.

UADataType.Description: Whether a deployment is bound to one immutable model version or follows a moving pointer. Stated structurally rather than as an upgrade policy, because what a client needs to know is whether the artefact can change under it, not what schedule someone intends to change it on.

Field.Name: Pinned
Field.Description: Bound to one immutable version. The artefact behind this deployment cannot change without an observable change to the deployment.

Field.Name: FollowsRef
Field.Description: Bound to a mutable pointer such as a branch or channel. The artefact CAN change without any other change, which is why clause 12 requires the resulting promotion to be as authorized as an explicit one.

UADataType.Description: Whether an import job brings the model's description or its bytes.

Field.Name: Federate
Field.Description: Materialize the catalogue entry as a ModelType and leave the artefact where it is. Nothing is downloaded and inference runs at the source.

Field.Name: Stage
Field.Description: Fetch the artefact, verify its Digest, and make it locally available so inference can run without the source.

Field.Name: Auto
Field.Description: Federate, then stage if the target deployment's InferenceLocation is OnServer or EdgeOffServer - because those cannot reach the source at inference time.

UADataType.Description: Severity of one safety finding. The scale is the convergent industry one; what each level means for a given category is the policy's business, not this specification's.
Whether the Server can currently reach a deployment's execution site.

Field.Name: Unknown
Field.Description: Never attempted, or the Server does not probe.

Field.Name: Reachable
Field.Description: The most recent attempt succeeded.

Field.Name: Unreachable
Field.Description: The most recent attempt failed.

Field.Name: Throttled
Field.Description: Reachable, but the endpoint is refusing work for capacity reasons. RetryAfter SHOULD be populated.

UADataType.Description: Stage of a chunked inference exchange. A client reads this rather than inferring progress from which Methods have succeeded, because a transfer that failed mid-write and one that has not started look alike from outside.

Field.Name: Building
Field.Description: The request is being written and is not yet complete.

Field.Name: Ready
Field.Description: The request is complete and inference has not started.

Field.Name: Executing
Field.Description: Inference is running.

Field.Name: Completed
Field.Description: The response is readable.

Field.Name: Failed
Field.Description: The exchange failed; LastError carries the reason.

Field.Name: Expired
Field.Description: The Server reclaimed the transfer before it completed.

UADataType.Description: Shape and element type of one model input or output tensor. This is what lets a client check that what it intends to send matches what the model expects, before it sends it.

Field.Name: Name
Field.Description: Tensor name as declared by the model.

Field.Name: ElementType
Field.Description: Element type, for example float32, uint8 or int64.

Field.Name: Shape
Field.Description: Dimensions; -1 marks a dynamic axis.

Field.Name: Layout
Field.Description: Optional axis layout hint, for example NCHW or NHWC.

UAObject.Description: Default Binary encoding of the structure.

UADataType.Description: Identity of a model as a publisher, name and version triple. Every model catalogue in practice identifies a model this way, which is why an import job takes this rather than a URL: a URL says where a copy is today, the triple says which artefact is meant.

Field.Name: Publisher
Field.Description: Organisation or namespace that published the model.

Field.Name: Name
Field.Description: Model name within that publisher.

Field.Name: Version
Field.Description: Immutable version identifier, or a mutable pointer such as a branch or channel name. Which one it is is stated by VersionBinding, not guessable from the string.

UAObject.Description: Default Binary encoding of the structure.

UADataType.Description: What one inference call consumed. Deliberately NOT named in tokens: a token is one accounting unit among several, and a model that consumes images, samples or seconds of audio needs the same accounting. UnitKind says which unit the counts are in.

Field.Name: UnitKind
Field.Description: Unit the counts are expressed in, for example 'tokens', 'images', 'samples' or 'seconds'.

Field.Name: InputUnits
Field.Description: Units consumed by the input.

Field.Name: OutputUnits
Field.Description: Units produced as output.

Field.Name: TotalUnits
Field.Description: Total units billed or metered for the call, which is not always the sum: cached or deduplicated input may be counted once.

UAObject.Description: Default Binary encoding of the structure.

UADataType.Description: One capability a deployment does or does not have. An open list rather than an enumeration because the set of things a model can do is not closed, and a client that cannot recognise a capability name is no worse off than one that cannot recognise an enumeration value it has never seen.

Field.Name: Name
Field.Description: Capability name, for example 'chat', 'embeddings', 'streaming', 'tool-call' or 'structured-output'.

Field.Name: Supported
Field.Description: Whether this deployment supports it.

UAObject.Description: Default Binary encoding of the structure.

UADataType.Description: One finding from a safety policy applied to an inference call. Category is a String and not an enumeration because harm categories are set by the policy an installation adopts, and an industrial taxonomy looks nothing like a consumer one.

Field.Name: Category
Field.Description: Category the policy assessed, for example 'out-of-distribution-input' or a policy-defined name.

Field.Name: Severity
Field.Description: Severity of the finding.

Field.Name: Filtered
Field.Description: True when the content was withheld or altered rather than merely flagged.

Field.Name: Detail
Field.Description: Human-readable explanation. For a human; SHALL NOT be parsed.

UAObject.Description: Default Binary encoding of the structure.

UADataType.Description: One measured metric from an evaluation run, with the threshold it was judged against. The threshold travels with the metric because a metric without its acceptance criterion cannot be acted on, and a reviewer reading it a year later has no way to recover what 'good' meant.

Field.Name: Name
Field.Description: Metric name, for example 'accuracy' or 'false-negative-rate'.

Field.Name: Value
Field.Description: Measured value.

Field.Name: Unit
Field.Description: Unit of the value, or empty when dimensionless.

Field.Name: Threshold
Field.Description: Acceptance threshold applied.

Field.Name: Comparison
Field.Description: How Value was compared with Threshold: one of '>=', '<=', '>', '<' or '=='.

Field.Name: Passed
Field.Description: Outcome of that comparison.

UAObject.Description: Default Binary encoding of the structure.

UADataType.Description: Capacity a remote endpoint is currently granting. Surfaced so a client can distinguish 'the model said no' from 'the quota said no', which are different faults with different remedies.

Field.Name: UnitKind
Field.Description: Unit the limit is expressed in, matching UsageDataType.UnitKind, or 'requests'.

Field.Name: Limit
Field.Description: Units permitted per interval, or 0 when not published.

Field.Name: Remaining
Field.Description: Units still available in the current interval.

Field.Name: Interval
Field.Description: Length of the interval the limit applies to.

Field.Name: RetryAfter
Field.Description: How long to wait before retrying. Zero when the endpoint gave no guidance.

UAObject.Description: Default Binary encoding of the structure.

UAReferenceType.Description: Links a Deployment to the Model it executes. Clause 6.5 requires exactly one such reference per deployment; it is the only defined path from a result to the model artefact and its Digest, on which the provenance requirement of clause 12 depends.

Links a Model to a Dataset it was trained or validated on. A model whose training data cannot be named is a model whose behaviour cannot be explained, which is why this reference exists rather than a string.

Links a Model to the Model it was fine-tuned, distilled or quantized from. Lineage is a chain, not a field: a model three derivations from its base is answerable for all three, and a string naming the immediate parent cannot be walked.
Links a Deployment to the Deployment that serves in its place when it cannot. Clause 9 forbids a cycle, and requires the response to say which deployment actually answered.
Links a Model to the catalogue resource an import job materialized it from. This is what makes 'where did this model come from' answerable after the fact, rather than only at the moment of import.
Links a Model to an EvaluationRun that measured it. Optional and repeating: a model may be evaluated many times, and the run that gated its promotion is not necessarily the last one.

UAObjectType.Description: Server-level entry point. A client that has just connected browses here to find every model, dataset, deployment and learning job the Server describes, without knowing its layout.

UAObject.Description: ModelType instances.
DatasetType instances.
DeploymentType instances.
LearningJobType instances.

UAVariable.Description: Release of this specification the Server implements, for example '0.1.0'.

UAObjectType.Description: Nameplate of a trained model. The member set is deliberately aligned with the IDTA 02060 AI Model Nameplate submodel template, which is currently the only standardised description of an industrial AI model, so an Asset Administration Shell can be populated from this node without loss.

UAVariable.Description: Identifier of the model.
Human-readable model name.
Model version.
Producing framework, for example PyTorch, TensorFlow or scikit-learn.
Serialization format, for example ONNX, TensorRT or OpenVINO IR.

What the model does, for example Detection2D, Classification, Segmentation, Forecasting or AnomalyDetection. Free text because the set of tasks is not closed and a closed enumeration would date faster than the model does.

Cryptographic digest of the model artefact, for provenance and integrity. Mandatory: clause 12 requires it for every model whose artefact is obtainable through ArtifactUri, and it is the terminus of the provenance chain that UsesModel keeps intact.

Hash function used for Digest. SHALL name a function with at least 256-bit output and no known collision weakness; SHA-256 is the default and is always acceptable. SHALL NOT be MD5, SHA-1 or a truncated variant - chosen-prefix collisions against those are practical, so a substituted artefact would pass verification. SHALL be non-empty where Digest is non-empty. See clause 12.
Where the model artefact can be obtained. Treated as untrusted input.
Training provenance or model card location.

Ordered class label set, where the model produces classified output. The INDEX is what a consuming specification's class identifier refers to, so the order is part of the contract and a Server SHALL NOT reorder it in place.
Input tensor signatures.
Output tensor signatures.

UAObjectType.Description: A dataset used to train or validate a model. Aligned with the IDTA 02058 AI Dataset submodel template. SourceKind distinguishes real capture from simulator output, which is the provenance a reviewer needs when synthetic data is involved.

UAVariable.Description: Identifier of the dataset.
Human-readable dataset name.
Dataset version.
Whether samples are real, synthetic or mixed.
Number of samples.
Class labels present.
Creation time.
Where the dataset can be obtained. Treated as untrusted input.
Digest of the dataset artefact.

UAObjectType.Description: A model made executable somewhere. Aligned with the IDTA 02059 AI Deployment submodel template. InferenceLocation is the on-server versus off-server switch: it changes where the computation happens and therefore the trust boundary, and it changes nothing else.

UAVariable.Description: Identifier of the deployment.
Where inference executes.
Compute device executing the model.
Free-text accelerator identification, for example an NPU or GPU part name.
Inference endpoint when InferenceLocation is not OnServer. Treated as untrusted input and subject to the resolver policy of clause 12.
Latency the deployment is expected to meet, so a client can detect regression.
Configured inference batch size.
Runtime state of the deployment.

UAObjectType.Description: One turn of the capture, label, train and promote loop. It exists so that corrections arriving from a consuming application have somewhere to accumulate and a defined path into a new model version. A Server may implement only the capture stages and leave training to an external MLOps system - the state machine is the same either way.

UAVariable.Description: Current stage of the loop. This is the PHASE, not the program lifecycle: the inherited CurrentState says whether the job is running, this says what it is doing. Clause 7 requires the two to agree.
Dataset being accumulated or used.
Model the job starts from.
Model produced by the job, awaiting promotion.
Samples accumulated so far, including corrections fed back.

UAMethod.Description: Begin accumulating samples and corrections into the dataset.
Request that a candidate model be trained from the collected dataset.

uax:Description.uax:Text: True when the request was queued.

UAMethod.Description: Promote the candidate model so that deployments begin using it. A Server SHALL require a distinct authorization for this Method: it changes what the equipment does without changing anything a reader of the address space would notice, which is precisely the change that needs a separate permission.

uax:Description.uax:Text: Deployment to update, or null for all.
The model now in use.

UAObjectType.Description: Abstract base of every long-running AI operation: learning, model import and asynchronous inference. It derives from the OPC 10000-10 ProgramStateMachineType, so the lifecycle - Ready, Running, Suspended, Halted - its transition events and its Start/Suspend/Resume/Halt Methods are inherited rather than reinvented, and every job in this model is auditable the same way.

UAVariable.Description: Identifier of the job, unique within the Server.
Diagnostic for the most recent failure. For a human; SHALL NOT be parsed.
When the job last entered Running.
When the job last left Running, or null while it is running.
Fraction complete, 0.0 to 1.0, or null where the job cannot estimate it. A Server SHALL NOT report a value it is guessing: null is informative, a fabricated 0.5 is not.
Identity that requested the job, recorded at the moment it started. Clause 12 requires this for any job that can promote a model.

UAObjectType.Description: Brings a model from a catalogue into this Server. It federates by default - materializing the catalogue entry as a ModelType whose artefact stays where it is - and stages the artefact when the target deployment could not otherwise reach it. Staging is the moment a substituted artefact would enter, which is why clause 10 requires the Digest to be verified there and nowhere else.

UAVariable.Description: ModelSourceType instance the model is pulled from.
Publisher, name and version being imported.
Whether to federate, stage, or decide from the target's InferenceLocation.
Deployment to create or update on success, or null to import the model without deploying it.
ModelType instance the job produced. Null until the job succeeds.
Artefact bytes fetched so far. Zero for a federating import, which moves none.
Whether the staged artefact's computed digest matched the one the catalogue declared. False on a staging import means the artefact SHALL NOT be deployed.

UAMethod.Description: Abandon the import. A partially staged artefact SHALL be discarded rather than left where a later deployment could pick it up.

UAObjectType.Description: One asynchronous inference request. It exists because not every inference returns while the caller waits: a batch scored overnight and a long analysis over recorded data are ordinary industrial cases, and modelling them as a Method that blocks for hours is not.

UAVariable.Description: Deployment executing the request.
Request body, encoded as RequestContentType states.
Media type of RequestPayload.
Response body once the job succeeds.
Media type of ResponsePayload.

Model that ACTUALLY executed the request, which is not always the one the deployment named when the job was submitted - a fallback or a followed reference can change it in between. The provenance chain of clause 12 walks this, not the deployment's current model.
What the call consumed.
Why the call stopped producing output.
Findings from the safety policy, if any were applied.

UAObjectType.Description: An externally hosted inference or catalogue endpoint this Server can reach. It carries everything needed to actually call something the Server did not deploy - the wire contract, how to authenticate, what the endpoint can do and whether it is answering - because a URI on its own is a string nobody can act on.

UAVariable.Description: Identifier of the source.
Base URI of the endpoint. Untrusted input, subject to the resolver policy of clause 12.
Wire contract the endpoint speaks.
Where the contract is documented. SHOULD be populated when ApiDialect is Proprietary, because otherwise nothing in the address space says how to call it.
How the Server authenticates itself to the endpoint.

Opaque handle naming the credential in whatever store the Server uses. It is a NAME, never a secret: clause 12 forbids a Server from exposing credential material through any Attribute of this model, and a client that can read this value learns only which credential is used, not what it is.
Audience or scope a bearer token is requested for, where AuthenticationKind is BearerToken.
Whether the Server can currently reach the endpoint.
When the endpoint last answered successfully.
Failures since the last success. Reset to zero on success.
Capacity the endpoint is currently granting.
What the endpoint reports it can do.

UAMethod.Description: Probe the endpoint and update Reachability. Defined so that a commissioning engineer can establish that credentials and network policy are right BEFORE a deployment depends on them, rather than discovering it from a failed inference.

uax:Description.uax:Text: Whether the probe succeeded.
Diagnostic. For a human.

UAMethod.Description: Enumerate the models the source offers.

uax:Description.uax:Text: Optional substring or expression; empty for all.
Upper bound on returned entries.
Publisher, name and version of each model offered.

UAObjectType.Description: One measurement of a model against a dataset. It is a first-class object and not a field on the model because the same model is evaluated many times, and because the run that gated a promotion has to remain readable afterwards to answer why the promotion was allowed.

UAVariable.Description: Identifier of the run.
Model that was measured.
Dataset the model was measured against.
When the run finished.
Measured metrics, each with the threshold it was judged against.
Whether every metric met its threshold. A Server SHALL NOT report true while any entry in Metrics has Passed false - a summary that disagrees with its own detail is worse than no summary.
Where the full report lives. Untrusted input, subject to clause 12.

UAObjectType.Description: What a human needs to decide whether a model may be used here: what it is for, where it stops working, and under what terms. Separate from the nameplate because a nameplate answers 'which artefact is this' and a card answers 'should this be running on my line'.

UAVariable.Description: What the model is for.
Where it is known not to work. Mandatory because a card that lists only capabilities is marketing, and the failure modes are the half a commissioning engineer needs.
Uses the supplier explicitly excludes.
Licence identifier or URI governing use of the artefact.
Latest date represented in the training data. A model cannot know about anything after this, which is often the explanation for a field failure.
Risks the supplier records.
Where to report a problem with the model.

UAObjectType.Description: A catalogue of models and the datasets they were trained on. It narrows the abstract registry's group placeholder to model publishers, so that a client browsing it knows what it will find rather than discovering it.

One publisher's namespace within a model registry: the organisation or project that released the models it contains. Publisher is the first element of the publisher/name/version triple by which every catalogue in practice identifies a model.

Abstract base of everything a model registry holds. It exists so that the inherited <Resource> placeholder can be narrowed ONCE to something that admits models and datasets and nothing else - a publisher holds both, and a placeholder can be overridden only by one declaration.

One model in a catalogue. Its versions are immutable and identified by content, so a version that has been seen cannot change meaning; mutable names such as a branch or a release channel are pointers AT versions, never versions themselves. Because the base type is a FileType, a Server that holds the artefact serves it through the inherited Open, Read and Close; one that only describes it leaves those unimplemented and points at the artefact instead.

UAVariable.Description: What the model does, for example 'object-detection' or 'anomaly-detection'. A String and not an enumeration, for the same reason it is one on ModelType: the set is not closed, and every catalogue in practice uses a free tag here.
Runtime or library the artefact targets.
Digest of the artefact this version names, as the catalogue declares it. A staging import compares its own computed digest with this and refuses on mismatch.
Algorithm of Digest. Subject to the strength requirement of clause 12.
Artefact size, so a staging import can decide whether it has room before it starts rather than after it fails.
Whether obtaining the artefact requires an acceptance or entitlement beyond ordinary authentication. A client that ignores this discovers it as a failure part-way through a staging import.
Mutable pointers this resource publishes - branches, tags or channels - that a deployment may follow instead of pinning. Naming them is what makes VersionBinding FollowsRef checkable.

UAObjectType.Description: One dataset in a catalogue, a sibling of ModelResourceType rather than something beneath it: a dataset outlives the models trained on it and is cited by several.

UAVariable.Description: Whether the samples are real, synthetic or mixed.
Samples in the dataset.
Digest of the dataset artefact as the catalogue declares it.
Algorithm of Digest.
Dataset size.

UAObject.Description: ModelSourceType instances - the externally hosted endpoints and catalogues this Server can reach.
ModelRegistryType instances this Server serves or mirrors.
EvaluationRunType instances.
Import and asynchronous inference jobs. Learning jobs remain under LearningJobs.
What a human needs to decide whether this model may run here.

UAVariable.Description: Organisation or namespace that published the model. With Name and Version this is the triple every catalogue identifies a model by, and it is what makes the same model recognisable across two installations that fetched it from different mirrors.
Parameters in the model, or 0 where not published. A crude but universally available proxy for what it will cost to run.

Numeric precision the artefact is stored in, for example 'fp32', 'int8' or 'fp8'. A quantized model is a DIFFERENT artefact with different behaviour, not a packaging detail, which is why it is stated rather than left to the format string.
Safety or content policy applied to this model's output, where one is. Untrusted input, subject to clause 12.
ModelSourceType instance this deployment executes through, where inference is not local. Null when InferenceLocation is OnServer.
Whether the deployment is pinned to an immutable model version or follows a mutable pointer.
The mutable pointer being followed, where VersionBinding is FollowsRef. Empty when Pinned.
What the Server does when this deployment cannot serve.
Whether the execution site is currently reachable. Always Reachable for an OnServer deployment that is not Faulted.
Failed calls since the last success.
When this deployment last answered successfully. With FallbackPolicy HoldLast this is how a caller judges whether the held answer is still worth having.
Capacity the execution site is currently granting.
What this deployment can do. A client checks here before calling a typed profile rather than discovering the answer from a rejection.

Where input data is processed, named in whatever scheme the operator uses - a site, a legal jurisdiction, or a named zone. This is the question a plant actually asks, and no amount of latency or accuracy data answers it.

Whether calling this deployment sends input data outside the operator's boundary. A Server SHALL set this true for every deployment whose InferenceLocation is Cloud, and SHALL NOT set it false merely because the channel is encrypted - the question is where the data goes, not who can read it in flight.

Whether the execution site retains input beyond serving the request, for example for provider-side logging or training. Unknown is not a value: a Server that cannot establish this SHALL report true, because the safe assumption is the one that keeps data in.
Where the governing data policy is documented.

UAMethod.Description:
Run inference and return the result. The payload is opaque here: what goes in and comes out is the consuming specification's vocabulary, and an envelope that tried to type it would have to be extended for every domain. What this Method fixes is everything AROUND the payload - routing, parameters, accounting, why it stopped, and which model actually ran.
The signature does not change with InferenceLocation. A deployment served from the Server's own process and one served from a remote service are called identically; the location changes the trust boundary and the latency, and nothing else.

uax:Description.uax:Text: Request body.
Media type of Payload.

Call parameters such as a sampling temperature or an output length bound. A Server SHALL reject a parameter it does not support rather than ignore it: a caller whose parameter was silently dropped believes it took effect.
How long the caller will wait. Zero means the Server's default.
Response body.
Media type of ResponsePayload.

The model that ACTUALLY produced this response. Not necessarily the one the deployment names now: a fallback answered from a different deployment, and a FollowsRef binding may have moved. The provenance chain of clause 12 walks this.
What the call consumed.
Why output stopped. A caller that ignores this will accept a truncated answer as a complete one.
Findings from the safety policy, if any applied.
How long to wait before retrying, where the failure was a capacity one. Zero when retrying immediately is as good as waiting, and meaningless when the failure was not retryable.

True when the deployment produced a response too large to return inline. ResponsePayload is then empty and the work is NOT lost - Transfer names where to read it. A client that ignores this reads an empty payload and concludes the model returned nothing.
InferenceTransferType instance holding the response, where TransferRequired is true. Null otherwise.

UAMethod.Description: Submit inference to be completed later, returning immediately with the job that will carry the result. For work that does not finish while a caller waits - a batch scored overnight, an analysis over recorded data.

uax:Description.uax:Text: Request body.
Media type of Payload.
Call parameters.
InferenceJobType instance tracking the request. The caller subscribes to it rather than polling.

UAMethod.Description: Report what this deployment can do, refreshed from the execution site rather than from cache. Defined because a remote endpoint's capabilities change without anything in this address space changing.

uax:Description.uax:Text: Current capabilities.

UAObject.Description: A publisher namespace held by this registry. Narrows the inherited placeholder so a model registry admits ModelPublisherType and nothing else.
A model or dataset published in this namespace. Narrows the inherited placeholder to this model's own resource types.

UAVariable.Description:
Largest request or response this deployment will carry inline through Invoke, in bytes. Zero means the deployment accepts no inline payload at all and BeginTransfer is the only way in.
A client reads this BEFORE calling rather than discovering the bound from a rejection, and a Server SHALL NOT publish a value larger than its own MaxByteStringLength, the negotiated MaxMessageSize or the Session's MaxResponseMessageSize permit - the smallest of those is the real limit and a client cannot see all of them.

UAMethod.Description: Opens a chunked exchange for a payload that will not fit inline, returning the InferenceTransferType instance to write into. This is the general path: Invoke is the shortcut that happens to work when everything is small.

uax:Description.uax:Text: Media type of the request body.
Expected request size in bytes, or 0 when not known in advance. A Server that cannot accommodate the stated size refuses here rather than after the client has uploaded it.
InferenceTransferType instance to write the request into.
False when the Server declined to open the exchange.

UAObject.Description: Entry point for the AI models this Server runs. A client browses Server/AiModelManagement/Models to find what this Server describes.

UAObjectType.Description:
One chunked inference exchange. It exists because Invoke carries its payload as a ByteString, and a ByteString is bounded by MaxByteStringLength, the negotiated MaxMessageSize and the Session's MaxResponseMessageSize - none of which the model gets to choose. An image, a point cloud or a window of high-rate samples exceeds those routinely, and a call that cannot carry the input is not a call.
Request and Response are Part 5 FileType objects: the client opens the request, writes it in chunks it selects, and closes it; after Execute the response is read the same way. Nothing here invents a transfer protocol, because OPC UA already has one and every client already implements it.

UAVariable.Description: Identifier of this exchange.
Stage the exchange has reached.

UAObject.Description: The request body, written by the client in chunks of its own choosing. Inference does not begin until Execute is called, so a partially written request is never acted on.
The response body, readable once State is Completed. Empty before that.

UAVariable.Description: Media type of the request body.
Media type of the response body.
The model that ACTUALLY produced the response, on the same terms as Invoke: a fallback or a followed reference can change it between the call and the read.
What the call consumed.
Why output stopped.
Findings from the safety policy, if any applied.
Diagnostic for the Failed state. For a human; SHALL NOT be parsed.

When the Server may reclaim this transfer if it has not completed. A client that abandons an exchange would otherwise hold Server resources until the Session ends, and a Server that never reclaimed them would be one denial of service away from unusable.

UAMethod.Description: Runs inference over the written request. The Method returns as soon as the request is accepted; State and the envelope members carry the outcome, which is what lets one exchange span a payload too large to have been a single call in the first place.

uax:Description.uax:Text: False when the request was incomplete or already executed.

UAMethod.Description: Abandons the exchange and releases what it holds. A client that has stopped caring about a response SHOULD say so rather than leaving the Server to wait out ExpiresAt.
